# Brief

M1b “fast path” is approved for computer use after M1a merges. It evaluates Decisions API multimodal gates, optionally Clef-flash, for step verification, page-state routing, early stopping, wait detection, and optional marked-element grounding. Confidence thresholds with big-model fallback are part of the design; injection detection is additive and does not replace the structural egress gate. The evaluation compares end-to-end latency and model calls per lookup against M1a.

Jev fit shadow mode compares Jev fit scores with historical outreach outcomes. Shadow-mode M1 consists of a typed outcome loader, temporal-quality inventory, deterministic sampling, synthetic validation, and a production dry run that makes no Jev calls; its local artifact records cohort coverage, point-in-time field coverage, estimated Jev usage, and estimated maximum cost. Shadow-mode M2 runs the frozen M1 cohort through Jev and produces a protected local report. The current M2 run scores Jev and Decisions; Terra execution is gated pending confirmation of its approximately $32 full-run cost, with a 1,000-pair sample estimated at approximately $6.50 as an alternative.

The Jev shadow scale-up freeze is complete and read-only: 499 outreaches across 20 organizations yielded 29,015 pairs and 40,523 shift rows, including 186 confirmed-exposure positive replies and 222 fillers. The protected artifact is outside the repository with restricted permissions; Jev plus Decisions scoring is estimated at $17.70, while Terra is estimated at approximately $267 and was not run. The v3 comparison remains small because only two v3 outreaches were retained. Review found blockers in non-timeout query-error handling and generation-aware bootstrap strata; the existing module structure remains suitable.

Admin-v3 surfaces are organized independently: the interactive surface does not import the scheduled surface, and scheduled-versus-interactive bundle selection belongs outside the individual surface builders. A review identified the cross-surface import and runtime surface predicate in the interactive bundle path as a package-organization violation.

The computer-use broker is merged in PR #19313 as `abd7f91db3e2d5c49b32fe74a63c335db07a56d6`; its unauthenticated broker path rejects requests, and direct TypeScript target-manifest execution is covered by regression validation. The earlier M0 demo was a false success because it accepted the broker's 502 error page as loaded content. PR #19400 fixes DNS address-list handling and preserves private-IP, metadata, rebinding, connected-peer, and credential-stripping protections; the live screenshot now shows the real Example Domain page. Security review remains NOT READY because missing-response and navigation-count guards lack executed tests and CONNECT coverage does not exercise the production adapter. Plain HTTP remains rejected.

The Jev three-way evaluation test suite has a type-safe `questions` list assertion at final head `61a438134c52844d90495e53160f3c2967448d09`, eliminating its scoped `ty` diagnostic without changing behavior.

Jev shadow-mode production query failures are required to avoid retaining SQL or database stderr in exception context; review at head `2fb68dca581082f1d9363257967b33f552e9e1ad` found that `raise ... from None` did not satisfy this invariant because the original subprocess exception remained in `__context__`.

At exact head `2fb68dca581082f1d9363257967b33f552e9e1ad`, review also validated the point-in-time memory lookup's indexed owner-row path and recorded index-only scans, while the exception-context leakage remained a blocking defect.

The Jev shadow-mode production-query invariant also covers traceback frame locals: at `c3bf2788`, `__cause__` and `__context__` were cleared, but SQL, command, and subprocess stderr remained reachable through the `select_json` traceback frame, so the review remained NOT READY despite passing tests and formatting.

The Admin-v3 computer-use infrastructure is merged across PRs #19302, #19313, and #19318. A real Vercel browser run loaded example.com through the egress broker, produced a view-only noVNC link that remained live for a 10-minute hold, and deleted the sandbox afterward. The implementation uses a dated Ubuntu snapshot with signature checks, SHA-256 verification for Chrome for Testing, a bounded hold duration, Vercel forwarding-CA trust without certificate bypass, and broker authentication that returns 403 for unauthenticated requests. The full egress matrix remains incomplete for private-IP and DNS-rebinding cases, and Admin-v3 M1 has not started.

The Admin-v3 deslop lane has a completed read-only planning artifact at `~/.zeta/scratch/admin_v3_deslop_plan.md`. The plan contains path-and-line evidence, a naming and persistence migration map, a limits audit, tool-set recommendations, shared-change boundaries, validation targets, and a seven-PR split. The first two behavior-neutral lanes, retiring rewrite scaffolding and using direct package-local names, have active workers; later lanes cover runtime simplification, query and write ownership, model-facing names, and interactive composition. The minimal tool-set question and other plan recommendations remain undecided, and no deslop removals are recorded.

Scheduled-automation milestone 2 covers management operations and concurrent-delete/fire fencing while preserving frozen policy JSON and excluding event-trigger support. PR #19221 merged into `main` as squash commit `b9b168e9d1` from approved head `9f20247f5bb5fb1ace0e6c20863d88c449ffaef7`; its event-dispatch guard is removed, its manual-run guard is retained, its applicable checks passed, its final review found no issues, and it had zero unresolved review threads. The follow-on milestone-2 management and delete/fire-fence implementation is active in a separate worktree.

On 2026-10-07, Henry approved the Admin-v3 deslop decisions: `codebase` remains for now; ordinary evidence file work and JSON slicing move toward the sandbox while durable artifact publication remains important; `render_dynamic_ui` remains as a prototype tool; the copied skills and framework skill tools remain; `run_bash` remains the model-facing name; persisted operation names make one clean cut from `admin_note.*`/`admin_page.*` to `note.*`/`page.*` with no permanent aliases and historical strings preserved in old runs and receipts; blocked and sales query actions are removed in favor of mounted capabilities and compact discovery; arbitrary query-shape caps and pre-spill truncation are removed while protective timeouts, provider limits, storage limits, approval expiry, and plan-evidenced windows remain; and the live port ledger, machine twin, and sync tests are deleted with a historical note retained.

On 2026-10-07, Henry also approved removing family-letter jargon and redundant `admin_`/`admin_v3_`/`admin_database_` prefixes across the Admin-v3 package, API route, worker composition, playground, prompts, skills, tests, docs, and model-facing names. The baseline contained 447 family-letter references: 316 in `tools/write`, 113 in `tools/query`, and the remainder in tests, interactive surfaces, and the API.

On 2026-10-08, the follow-up Jev evaluation was approved after M2's inconclusive real-outcome evidence. The approved scale-up uses an approximately 500-outreach, 20-or-more-organization cohort capped at 50,000 pairs, with an expected minimum of 50 positive replies and 50 placement fillers; it scores Jev and Decisions only after the request-size fix, at an estimated cost of approximately $30. Terra is excluded because its estimated cost is approximately $460 and remains unapproved. The request-size fix and read-only cohort-freezing work are running in parallel on `henry/jev-recommendations`.

On 2026-10-05, a computer-use landscape research artifact was completed. Its caveated findings describe strong short-task benchmark performance but substantially harder long workflows, continued prompt-injection risk, increasing use of hybrid GUI and code/API actions, and poor comparability across benchmark harnesses, step limits, task versions, and tool access. The artifact distinguishes sourced, inferred, unverified, and self-reported claims.

The Jev request-size fix was merged into `henry/jev-recommendations` as `f43a988e79` after review found no issues. Oversized pairs are split into one request per dimension instead of being dropped, and each pair records whether scoring used one request or split requests. Two additional 50-case, three-repeat golden runs completed 150/150 attempts each at 78.12% and 79.17% playbook exactness; the earlier approximately 73% result was attributed to provider variance. The focused review passed 148 tests, and the follow-up scale-up cohort freeze remains in progress.

Henry's direction for the Admin-v3 SQL query tool is to port the v3 agent's query tool with the same SQL-against-an-entity-catalog design, validation, and scope rewrite, while giving the Admin-v3 agent a much wider catalog and the ability to work across organizations. The proposed plan includes automatic entity specs from the existing `admin_readable_schema_catalog.json`, explicit organization scope including an all-organizations option, structural exclusion of credential columns, sandbox spilling instead of truncation for row caps, and removal of the typed-expression compiler and most internal named sources while retaining providers such as Linear, GitHub, and Calendar as named sources. This direction replaces deslop PR 4.

The agent query path is organized as validate, rewrite, run, and serialize. Row scope is applied within the execution pipeline and cannot be bypassed by caller-provided arguments; an organization or mode outside the run's scope produces a refusal rather than broader query access. Trusted execution options include frozen-at timestamps, bindings, row limits, and remainder counting, and are distinct from model-provided SQL arguments.

The v3 agent and Admin-v3 interactive run bundle both pass a run-derived `prompt_cache_key` into model policy, using the same prompt-cache-key mechanism. Henry's rationale for the SQL port is that it will make the v3 Admin agent less restricted and let it control its own queries, reducing repeated tool calls.

The computer-use optimization research reports that deterministic browser signals should precede model gates for page state, early-stop gates are the riskiest gate, and a gate should not independently terminate a lookup. Recommended validation combines visible-text, URL, and typed-value checks with large-model escalation when signals disagree. The research also reports that checked URL templates plus page-text extraction can reduce read-only lookup cost and latency, DOM or accessibility references generally provide stronger grounding than image marks, and evaluation should measure end-to-end latency and model calls rather than gate speed alone. Decisions API status was reported as public beta on 2026-10-06, with the gate value for screenshot web agents still requiring project-local trace validation.

PR #19388's earlier wrong-host remediation completed at exact head `885e82270c610ec7fd36ff74d6ef2b250dbc9b23`. Subsequent review fixes were verified live at current head `540ffefad50015a6ceed53b94433a631a7b00d61`: broker redirects are delegated to Chrome with both redirect hops retained in provenance, default session construction works, the idle-timer race is fixed, `click` performs a real click, and the hidden one-hour cap is removed. Example Domain, a crates.io search, and a cross-host redirect passed live validation; focused browser and broker validation passed, cleanup found no matching sandboxes, and the worktree is clean. Strict re-review is running and PR #19388 is not merged.

The completed UI-parity investigation found that customer v3 lives under `apps/web/features/phoebe_chat_v3/**` and Admin-v3 under `apps/web/features/admin_v3_playground/**`. The surfaces share `ui/primitives/generated_table.tsx` but otherwise use different event protocols, projections, cards, and styling. **Superseded on 2026-10-08:** the recommended architecture of separate conversation shells with a versioned typed `UiBlockEnvelope`, one neutral frontend block registry, shared rendering components, and surface-owned host adapters is no longer the active implementation plan. The active direction is a full one-to-one copy of the customer v3 transcript UI into Admin-v3, without shared imports, so the Admin-v3 copy can diverge later. The backend prerequisite is an Admin-v3 event-feed endpoint using exactly the customer v3 NDJSON protocol, event shapes, cursor, and resume behavior, with the projection copied into Admin-v3 code and Admin-only details represented as optional fields. A subsequent frontend PR copies `apps/web/features/phoebe_chat_v3/**` into the Admin-v3 playground, points it at the new feed, and removes the old Admin-v3 stream path; customer v3 remains untouched. The read-only plan is recorded at `~/.zeta/scratch/admin_v3_ui_parity_plan.md`.

The completed read-only persistent-sandbox study recommends dedicated Admin-v3 Modal compute with a Modal Volume working filesystem and S3 as the canonical backup. The study found that this preserves the existing sandbox's deny-all egress, isolation, mutation fencing, audit, and cost telemetry while allowing `/repo` to replace the specialized `codebase` tool. An immortal Modal sandbox process was rejected because its session lifetime is limited to 24 hours and it provides no additional filesystem durability. EC2 with Regional EFS and S3 backups was identified as a stronger but heavier alternative, estimated at approximately `$14–42/month` and 4–8 engineering weeks at the studied storage sizes. No implementation resources were created by the study.

For the computer-use foundations evaluation, Henry prefers using an existing public site that already evaluates computer-use capabilities rather than building a custom fixture site while computer use remains experimental. Storage state, telemetry destination, and evaluation budget were delegated to the project's recommendations; no specific choices for those three items are recorded yet.

The computer-use foundations reliability gate is defined around public sites whose stated purpose permits automation or scraping, synthetic identifiers and invented data, a clear Phoebe eval User-Agent, serial per-site low-rate execution, honored `robots.txt`, and preflight of every task URL through its complete redirect chain. HTTPS is required at the initial URL and every redirect hop; downgrade, TLS failure, or unchecked URL blocks the task. Scoring relies on page-side event receipts, page state, httpbin response echoes, broker request receipts, and controlled egress listeners rather than controller target claims or child “done” text. Recovery that cannot determine whether a non-idempotent effect occurred records `effect_unknown`, cleans up the sandbox, and stops without replaying the action. The evaluated public-site set includes The Internet, Expand Testing, httpbin, and Books to Scrape, with disallowed paths and unavailable-site conditions treated as coverage constraints.
